messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to check the significance for fixed effects in INLA model
parts:
On Mon, 2019-10-07 at 22:10 -0700, Nurul Syafiah Abd Naeeim wrote:
> How to check the significance for fixed effects in INLA model
>

as in any Bayesian model. with an informative prior for that fixed
effect, you can compare the log marginal likelihood (result$mlik),
and/or look at the credibility interval for that coefficient.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to check the significance for fixed effects in INLA model
parts:
I compute the the confidence interval,
exp.b0.mean=inla.emarginal(exp,Model$marginals.fixed[[1]])
exp.b0.95CI=inla.qmarginal(c(0.025,0.975),inla.tmarginal(exp,Model$marginals.fixed[[1]]))

exp.b1.mean=inla.emarginal(exp,Model$marginals.fixed[[2]])
exp.b1.95CI=inla.qmarginal(c(0.025,0.975),inla.tmarginal(exp,Model$marginals.fixed[[2]]))

exp.b2.mean=inla.emarginal(exp,Model$marginals.fixed[[3]])
exp.b2.95CI=inla.qmarginal(c(0.025,0.975),inla.tmarginal(exp,Model$marginals.fixed[[3]]))

exp.b3.mean=inla.emarginal(exp,Model$marginals.fixed[[4]])
exp.b3.95CI=inla.qmarginal(c(0.025,0.975),inla.tmarginal(exp,Model$marginals.fixed[[4]]))

then how about the credible interval?

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to check the significance for fixed effects in INLA model
parts:
Credible intervals are what one gets from quantiles of the posterior, as in the code shown. Confidence intervals are defined from the sampling distribution of a point estimator, and requires other methods to compute. It is not only a matter of different interpretation.

Confidence intervals are well defined even in Bayesian contexts, and are quite separate from credible intervals; they may be close in practice, but have completely separate definitions.

Finn

parts:
Unless you're trying to assess frequentistic properties of Beysian
methods, don't bother about confidence intervals at all. Just use the
credible intervals that the Bayesian procedure provides (via the
inla.qmarginal() calls that you listed).

Finn

Simon Jackman (author of Bayesian Analysis for Social Sciences @ Stanford U.) provides a cogent graphic for Bayesian vs Frequentist Inference that I believe everyone may keep in mind when they do either forms (freq or Bayes):

https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/8870/46ae39f2c9d8eba3fb85008c0a047b3484fd.pdf

especially this slide:


Problem is, frequentists never have to defend their methods but Bayesians do ...

Regards,

Rudy B.
